body.en: A vector has both magnitude and direction. Vectors model force, velocity, and displacement. Parametric equations describe motion and curves by expressing both coordinates as functions of a parameter \(t\).

For \(\mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle\) and \(\mathbf{v}=\langle v_1,v_2\rangle\), scalar \(k\):

\[\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}=\langle u_1+v_1,u_2+v_2\rangle,\quad k\mathbf{u}=\langle ku_1,ku_2\rangle,\]\[|\mathbf{u}|=\sqrt{u_1^2+u_2^2},\quad\hat{\mathbf{u}}=\frac{\mathbf{u}}{|\mathbf{u}|}\quad(\text{unit vector}).\]

Component form from magnitude/angle: \(\mathbf{v}=\langle|\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta,\;|\mathbf{v}|\sin\theta\rangle.\)

body.en:
Curve: \(x=f(t),\;y=g(t).\)

Method 1: solve for \(t\) from one equation, substitute into the other.

Method 2 (trig): if \(x=a\cos t\) and \(y=b\sin t\), use \(\cos^2t+\sin^2t=1\Rightarrow\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1.\)

Projectile motion: \(x=v_0\cos\alpha\cdot t,\quad y=v_0\sin\alpha\cdot t-\tfrac{1}{2}g t^2.\)

problem.en: Convert \(x=3\cos t,\;y=5\sin t,\;t\in[0,2\pi]\) to Cartesian form.
A ball is kicked at 20 m/s at 60° to the horizontal. Find: (a) max height, (b) range, (c) time of flight.

solution.en:
\(v_x=20\cos60°=10\text{ m/s},\quad v_y=20\sin60°=10\sqrt3\text{ m/s}.\)

(a) At max height \(v_y=0\): \(t_{\text{top}}=10\sqrt3/9.8\approx1.77\text{ s}.\quad H=10\sqrt3(1.77)-\frac12(9.8)(1.77)^2\approx15.3\text{ m}.\)

(b) Time of flight: \(T=2t_{\text{top}}\approx3.53\text{ s}.\quad\text{Range}=10(3.53)\approx35.3\text{ m}.\)

label.en: ▲ Pre-Calculus Traps & Commandments — Vectors & Parametric Equations

body.en:
• Dot Product Output: The dot product \(\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2\) yields a scalar (a single number), never a vector. Writing component brackets around the dot product is a major conceptual error.
  • Vector vs. Scalar Projection: Scalar projection is the signed magnitude \(\text{comp}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{u} = \frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{v}|}\). Vector projection incorporates direction: \(\text{proj}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{u} = \frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{v}|^2}\,\mathbf{v}\). Notice that the denominator is \(|\mathbf{v}|^2\) in the vector projection.
  • Parametric Domain Restrictions: When eliminating \(t\) to find a Cartesian equation, always record the natural domain and range restricted by the parameter. For instance, \(x = 2\cos t\) limits \(x\) to \([-2, 2]\).
  • Orthogonal vs. Parallel Conditions: Two nonzero vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if \(\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0\). They are parallel if and only if \(\mathbf{u} = k\mathbf{v}\) (their components are strictly proportional).

question.en: Given vectors \(\mathbf{a} = 2\mathbf{i} - 5\mathbf{j}\) and \(\mathbf{b} = -3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}\), find the scalar projection of \(\mathbf{a}\) onto \(\mathbf{b}\) and the angle \(\theta\) between them to the nearest tenth of a degree.

solution.en:
Calculate the dot product:

\[\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = (2)(-3) + (-5)(4) = -6 - 20 = -26.\]

Calculate the magnitudes:

\[|\mathbf{a}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-5)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 25} = \sqrt{29} \approx 5.385,\]\[|\mathbf{b}| = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5.\]

Scalar projection of \(\mathbf{a}\) onto \(\mathbf{b}\):

\[\text{comp}_{\mathbf{b}}\mathbf{a} = \frac{\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}}{|\mathbf{b}|} = \frac{-26}{5} = -5.2.\]

Angle \(\theta\) between vectors:

\[\cos\theta = \frac{\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}}{|\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|} = \frac{-26}{5\sqrt{29}} \approx -0.9656 \implies \theta = \arccos(-0.9656) \approx 164.9°.\]

question.en: Eliminate the parameter to determine the Cartesian equation of the curve \(x = 1 + 2\sec t\), \(y = -2 + 3\tan t\). State the shape, center, and vertices.

solution.en:
Isolate the trigonometric terms:

\[\sec t = \frac{x - 1}{2}, \qquad \tan t = \frac{y + 2}{3}.\]

Apply the fundamental Pythagorean identity \(\sec^2 t - \tan^2 t = 1\):

\[\left(\frac{x - 1}{2}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{y + 2}{3}\right)^2 = 1 \implies \frac{(x - 1)^2}{4} - \frac{(y + 2)^2}{9} = 1.\]

This is a horizontal hyperbola with:

  • Center: \((h, k) = (1, -2)\)
  • Transverse semi-axis: \(a = 2\)
  • Vertices: \((h \pm a, k) = (1 \pm 2, -2) = (-1, -2)\) and \((3, -2)\)
